title: Capture status file
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.5, #773), not implemented. `/run/sizeup-radio/status.json`: what capture OBSERVES, written by capture (its only writer) as compact JSON with tmp + rename every 0.5 s and at once when something changes. Never a reply (those are on the socket) and never a wish. A reader takes capture as down when its own CLOCK_BOOTTIME is 15 s or more past `at_boot`, or when `boot` is not its own boot id (a file left from before a reboot); `at` is for people. The app builds today's radio status, dongle rows and health rows from this file plus its own; it carries no secret.

at.description: When capture wrote the file, Unix seconds (wall clock): for people.

at_boot.description: The same moment on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, seconds since boot: what staleness is measured from.

boot.description: The boot id `at_boot` belongs to. Opaque: compared for equality only.

impl.description: The implementation: `python`, or a native daemon's name.

contract.description: The capture contract's major version capture speaks, 1.

started.description: When this capture process started, Unix seconds.

wish_seq.description: The `seq` of the wish capture runs; 0 while it has accepted none (it idles).

wish_problem.description: Why a newer wish file could not be read at all (capture keeps running the last one it accepted); "" when fine.

refusals.description: The parts of the applied wish that failed validation and were NOT applied; [] when the wish runs as written. An entry stays until a wish without the fault is applied.

items.title: One refused part
items.description: One part of a wish capture did not apply; it keeps running what it ran for that part.

key.description: Which one: a dongle's serial, a group's name, a channel's label; "" when the part has no key.

wish_seq.description: The `seq` of the wish the refusal is about.

reader.title: The reader
reader.description: Whether an app holds the socket as `reader`.

attached.description: A client that said `role` `reader` is connected.

since.description: Since when it is attached, or has been gone, Unix seconds; null when never.

channels.description: One row per channel of the set.

items.title: One channel
items.description: One channel of the set: what it is doing now.

mhz.description: The frequency it is on, MHz; null when it is on none.

sdr.description: The serial of the dongle it runs on; "" when it runs on none.

run.description: The channel's running state, in the words of docs/nodes.md (`capabilities.channels[].state`): `running`; `waiting` (no dongle, by choice or for lack of one); `out` (a dongle streaming nothing, #710); `held` (another app holds its dongle); `shed` (to a higher job of its group); `not_in_set`; `local` (a person's override). A reader takes a word it does not know as not running.

detail.description: A sentence for people about the state.

restarts.description: How many times the receiver's program was restarted since capture started.

open_s.description: How long the squelch has been open without a break, seconds; null when closed.

stuck.description: Open for longer than a transmission can be.

last_heard.description: When it last received something, Unix seconds; null for never.

queued.description: Transmissions that closed and wait for capture's worker: not yet on the spool. A count.

quieting_db.description: How far the noise is quieted now, dB; null when not measured.

hiss_db.description: The idle hiss the quieting is measured from, relative dB; null until measured.

floor_db.description: The channel's noise floor, relative dB; null until measured.

squelch.description: The squelch as it runs now: what a `squelch_apply` request's `expect` is compared with.

now.description: Airband: the frequencies it is on now, in words.

ab.description: Airband: an on-air A/B comparison's state while one runs. Not typed here.

items.title: One dongle
items.description: One RTL-SDR dongle, as a row of today's `App.sdr()`, with `job` for today's `mode`. The group fields (`group`, `own`, `for`, `on`) are as in station-state.schema.json.

name.description: Its name here (the serial when none was given).

product.description: Its USB product name; "" when it is not plugged in.

job.description: The job it runs or is set to, or `Off`.

set_by.description: Who chose its job: `person` (the wish), `auto` (capture's auto-assign: the app mirrors it into its own record), or null (a default).

held_by.title: Another application's claim
held_by.description: Who else holds the dongle; null when nobody.

mode.description: What it says it uses the dongle for.

noaudio.description: The dongle opens but streams no audio (#710); null otherwise.

ambiguous.description: Why nothing may open it now (two dongles share its serial); "" when fine.

lent.description: While a reception test has the dongle; null otherwise.

group.description: Its antenna group's name; absent outside groups.

own.description: A stand-in only: its own job, kept aside while it runs another's.

for.description: A stand-in only: the dongles it stands in for.

on.description: Its job runs on this stand-in dongle instead.

groups.description: The antenna groups as they run, as `App.sdr()` gives them; [] when there are none. Not typed here.

groups_problem.description: Why the groups were dropped; "" when fine.

no_park.description: The jobs that may not be parked.

duplicates.description: Serials two or more dongles share; [] for none.

adsb.description: The dongle reserved for the ADS-B receiver, as `App.sdr()` gives it. Not typed here.

p25.description: The P25 systems, by short name.

additionalProperties.title: One P25 system
additionalProperties.description: The trunk-recorder side of one system.

detail.description: A sentence for people about the state.

cc.description: The control channel (`ControlChannel.status()`): decode rate, retunes. Not typed here.

last_call.description: When the last call was taken, Unix seconds; 0 for none.

mark.description: The replay mark (#753): calls that ended before it are done, Unix seconds; null for none.

seen.description: The size of the ingest's set of seen calls, a count: bounded (the soak test).

reception.description: `Tests.state()`: the running reception test and the history. The app shows it; it runs nothing of the test. Not typed here.

pending.description: Items not yet acknowledged by the reader's cursor, a count.

oldest_s.description: The age of the oldest unacknowledged item, seconds; 0 when there is none.

bytes.description: The spool's size on disk, bytes.

free_bytes.description: Free space on the spool's filesystem, bytes.

dropped.description: Spool writes that failed (the disk was full), a count.

dropped_audio.description: Items whose audio was dropped at a bound or under the reserve, a count.

synced_at.description: When the spool was last synced to disk, Unix seconds; null for never.

urgent.title: The urgent lane
urgent.description: The urgent file and its senders, for Health and for the station's own "EMERGENCY not delivered to the hub" banner. "Unsent" is the senders' own view, not the rows' states.

urgent_epoch.description: The urgent file's epoch, 16 hex characters.

mode.description: The urgent-mode in effect: `write` or `send`, never `off` (the file's `off` is `write` in service mode).

state.description: The senders' condition, one word: the FIRST of these that holds. `off` (not sending: the mode is not `send`, the wish's `hub.forward` is false, or the hub does not advertise `urgent`); `no_credentials` (no token in the credential store: capture does everything but send); `no_route` (404, 405: a hub without the route); `refused` (401, 403, 409: `reason` has the hub's word); `retrying` (no answer, a timeout, 502, 503, 530, 429); `ok`. A reset of the urgent file is not a state (`resets`). A reader takes a word it does not know as not ok.

reason.description: With `refused`: the hub's `reason` word; "" otherwise. Never a body, never a token.

pending.description: Items not yet answered for, alarms and pages, a count.

pending_alarms.description: Alarms not yet answered for, a count.

unsent.description: The alarms the hub has not answered for, oldest first, and the alarms this lane gave up on (`rejected`) that the hub does not have by the app's lane yet: what the station's page shows as not delivered once one is 10 s old.

items.title: One unsent alarm
items.description: An alarm the hub has not answered for.

unit.description: The radio's alias; "" when it has none.

age_s.description: Its age when the file was written, seconds, on the boot clock within a boot.

undurable.description: Items that live in memory only (no row: a failed insert, a stalled disk), a count.

oldest_alarm_s.description: The age of the oldest unsent alarm, seconds; null when there is none.

last_sent_at.description: When the hub last answered for an item, Unix seconds; null for never.

last_ms.description: How long the last answered request took, hand-over to answer, milliseconds; null for none.

sent.description: Items the hub answered for (`applied`, `duplicate`, `stale`) since capture started, a count.

rejected.description: Items that ended `rejected` since capture started (a `rejected` in a 200, a lone 422, 5 answers it could not read), a count. A rejected alarm still rides the app's lane, and Health is critical for it.

expired.description: Page items that expired unsent (120 s) since capture started, a count. Alarms never expire.

last_error.description: The last failure: a status and the hub's reason, never a body, never a token; "" for none.

hub_gen.description: The hub's fencing generation in its last answer (lease.schema.json `counter`); null before the first.

creds_at_boot.description: When the credentials were last taken (at start, or by a reload), on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, seconds since boot; null when there are none.

p25_transitions_1h.description: P25 emergency-bit transitions in the last hour (#775), a count: a misbehaving radio or decoder shows here.

resets.description: How often the urgent file was unreadable at start and replaced by a new one (a new `urgent_epoch`) since capture started, a count.

reset_at.description: When the last such reset was, Unix seconds; null for none. Health shows a reset for 24 h.

open_db.description: The squelch opens at this much quieting, dB.

close_db.description: The squelch closes below this much quieting, dB.
